sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (unitary national jurisdiction; registry seat in Majuro Atoll)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: United States common-law and constitutional influence, code-based corporate statutes, and customary law; the Business Corporations Act is modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the United States and the Republic of the Marshall Islands (1986; Amended Compact in force 2003; economic provisions renegotiated 2023)
Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York, 1958) — RMI accession 2007, relevant to charter party and bunker supply dispute resolution
No comprehensive double taxation agreement or bilateral investment treaty in force as of the due-diligence date

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act, 27 MIRC Chapter 3, as amended (2024 consolidation), administered by the Registrar of Associations; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2019, as amended, together with the regulations and FIU directives issued thereunder; Registered Agents Act (licensing, AML/CFT and record-keeping obligations of registered agents); Maritime Act 1990, as amended (maritime licensing and vessel-calling framework); Banking Act 1991, as amended (payment systems and banking-license context). The beneficial-ownership regime requires each licensed registered agent to obtain, verify, and maintain the identity of every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding 25% or more of equity, voting rights, or effective control, together with the full control chain, and to maintain the UBO record at the registered office while the statutory records remain non-public.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy issued by the Registrar of Associations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Associations, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (issued through the licensed registered agent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (certified copy, including registered office and registered agent clauses)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Associations, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Associations, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO and Directors Statutory Declaration (AML/CFT extract with complete beneficial-ownership chain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of signing, certified by the licensed registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency (identity of directors, officers, and registered agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed registered agent / corporate secretary of the entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening, at onboarding and continuously thereafter, of all shareholders, directors, officers, UBOs, signatories, counterparties, and vessels/charterers against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT OFSI Consolidated List, and RMI domestic counter-terrorism designations; foreign and domestic PEPs are identified per FATF Recommendation 12, requiring enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval. The medium-risk enhanced tier applicable to the ISIC 5222 bunkering scope requires automated screening of World-Check-grade quality, adverse-media review, and documentary verification of corporate vehicles and ultimate controllers. The Republic of the Marshall Islands was removed from the FATF grey list in June 2021 and remains in Asia/Pacific Group (APG) follow-up; registered agents must retain CDD records for at least five years after the end of the business relationship. For maritime operations, the RMI Maritime Administrator (International Registries, Inc.) additionally performs integrity vetting of vessel owners, bunker suppliers, and operators under the Maritime Act 1990.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Corporate Registry Online e-Services of the Registrar of Associations, Office of the Registrar, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (filings may be submitted directly or through licensed registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate filings and the corporate name must be in English, the official working language of the Registry; the name must be composed of Latin-alphabet characters and standard typographic symbols. Foreign-language names require an English transliteration and must not create a conflict with existing registered names. The name must end with a statutory corporate suffix (e.g., 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited' or accepted abbreviations such as 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Banker', 'Banking' (requires Banking Commissioner license prior to registration)

'Government', 'National', 'Federal', 'Republic', 'Presidential', 'Ministerial' and any token implying state sponsorship or connection with the Republic of the Marshall Islands Government or head of state
'Chamber of Commerce', 'University', 'Cooperative', 'Building Society', 'Exchange', 'Stock Exchange' (requires prior approval of the competent authority)
Tokens identical or confusingly similar to any existing name on the Register of Associations (automatic refusal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a written refusal notice from the Registrar of Associations, the applicant or its licensed registered agent may file a written administrative appeal within 14 calendar days of receipt, stating legal grounds, annexing the refusal notice, and paying the appeal processing fee (statutory tariff). The Registrar must issue a written decision within 30 days. A second refusal may be challenged by judicial review in the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the Administrative Procedure Act, with an application filed within 30 days of the final administrative decision. Extension of a name reservation: a written extension request lodged before expiry may, at the Registrar's discretion, renew the reservation for a further 30-day window; if no extension is granted, the name re-enters the available pool and a fresh search and fee are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the non-resident business corporation: the Business Corporations Act requires only a registered office and a licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands and does not require a physical operational presence. For the ISIC 5222 marine bunkering and fuel-supply scope, the virtual registered office is accepted for registry purposes; however, the statutory bunkering/fuel-supply license, flag-state obligations under the Maritime Act 1990, ISPS port requirements, and the AML risk-tier requirements of retaining banks and Standby LC counterparties will impose a separate commercial-substance and operations-presence assessment in the port state where fueling operations actually occur. The RMI entity itself may remain a pure holding and supply-contract vehicle.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the registered office: quantified residual risk of an unannounced inspection by the Registrar of Associations is estimated at under 5% per annum. Enhanced for operations: for RMI-flag vessels or bunkering operations calling at US, EU, and Asia-Pacific ports, the probability of Port State Control and RMI Maritime Administrator integrity inspections rises to an estimated 30-40% per vessel-year, and any physical corporate presence in a foreign port state may trigger local licensing audits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search, clearance, and 30-day name reservation fee (first name, with alternative names on review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Associations, Republic of the Marshall Islands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business Corporation incorporation filing fee (non-resident domestic corporation; scale based on authorized share capital up to USD 1,000,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Associations, Republic of the Marshall Islands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copies of Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation (first issuance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Associations, Republic of the Marshall Islands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent and registered office services, year 1 (including corporate register, share ledger, and statutory filings)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed RMI registered agent (corporate service provider)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding and UBO file setup: KYC/CDD, beneficial-ownership profiling, PEP and sanctions screening (automated screening and adverse-media research)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent's AML compliance officer / external screening data provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and drafting: articles of incorporation, by-laws, UBO statutory declaration, directors' resolutions, and bank-account authorization pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External counsel authorized in the Republic of the Marshall Islands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and consular legalization of the incorporation and UBO document bundle (RMI is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; authentication through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consular channel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs / consular authentication office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus prevailing notarial fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Maritime regulatory advisory for the ISIC 5222 bunkering scope: licensing eligibility under the Maritime Act 1990 and correspondence with the RMI Maritime Administrator (International Registries, Inc.) for fuel-supply counterparty vetting
Certificate of Good Standing (three certified copies, post-incorporation) and courier/disbursements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Associations and international courier service

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Title 27, RMI Revised Code 2004 (as amended); sections 27-101 (Incorporators), 27-201 (Filing of Articles of Incorporation), 27-301 (Registered Office and Registered Agent) and 27-206 (General Powers and Amendment of Articles).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Commerce and Trade, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro; international filings are accepted through licensed Marshall Islands registered agents and authorised service centres of the Maritime Administrator.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Registrar of Corporations form MHC-1) together with the written consent of the registered agent (form MHC-3).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Business Corporations Act; the Articles may authorise a nominal capital, commonly 1,000 shares at USD 1.00 par value. No pre-incorporation escrow account or bank deposit is required by the Registrar of Corporations; the subscribed consideration may remain unpaid until called, and the corporation may lawfully commence business upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's subscription for 1,000 shares of authorized capital stock, par value USD 1.00 per share, is accepted; the Secretary shall issue share certificate(s) upon payment of the consideration. RESOLVED, that the registered office at the registered agent's Majuro address is adopted, and that agency for service of process is ratified. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer respectively, to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the corporate seal is approved; the officers are authorized to open bank and correspondent accounts, execute bunkering and fuel-supply contracts, obtain bunkering permits, and take all steps to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (submission through a licensed registered agent or the registrar's e-filing portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-reservation request for the proposed corporate name together with two alternative names. The Registrar verifies that the proposed name is distinguishable from existing corporations and does not contain prohibited terms such as bank, trust or insurance unless a financial-services licence is held. A name reservation certificate is issued upon approval.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (Register form MHC-2)
Proposed corporate name and two alternates
Applicant identification or authorising resolution
Registered agent instruction letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, promptly re-file the reservation with an alternate name. If the reserved name is later refused upon incorporation, amend the Articles to a permitted name and re-file within the reservation validity window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sole incorporator and notary public; document is reviewed by the Registrar of Corporations upon filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in English stating the corporate name, the registered office and agent address in the Marshall Islands, the authorised share capital and par value, and any lawful limitations on purposes or duration. Execute the Articles before a notary or by an equivalent consent declaration; the incorporator also subscribes for the initial shares.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (form MHC-1) executed by the incorporator
Consent of the registered agent (form MHC-3)
Subscription agreement or incorporator's resolution
Notarisation certificate, if executed outside the Republic
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies a drafting defect at filing, withdraw and execute corrected Articles, then re-file; defects in an already filed certificate are cured by filing a certificate of correction under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles with the Registrar and Pay Filing Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the executed Articles, the name reservation certificate and the registered agent consent to the Registrar together with the applicable statutory filing fee per the current fee schedule. The Registrar stamps the instrument, issues the certificate of incorporation and records the filing; corporate existence commences on the date of issuance.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation
Name reservation certificate
Registered agent consent
Filing fee remittance or payment reference
Registrar intake sheet (form MHC-0), if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried by a written deficiency notice, cure the stated defect by filing a certificate of correction within 30 days; failure to cure may void the reservation, requiring a fresh application and fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold First Board Meeting and Adopt Organizational Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the Corporation; no government filing is required for internal acts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an organisational meeting of the board of directors or act by unanimous written consent. The board adopts the pro-forma First Board Resolution, approves the bylaws, elects officers, fixes the fiscal year and authorises the opening of bank accounts. Minutes or the unanimous consent must be signed by all incumbent directors.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent of directors or organisational meeting minutes
Bylaws approved by the board
Officer and director consent or oath forms
Pro-forma First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any organisational act is later found defective, the full board may ratify it by a curative unanimous written consent; ratification is effective retroactively and requires no registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate Registered Agent Service, Issue Shares and Maintain the Share Ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent and the Corporation's corporate secretary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm in writing the registered office address, the statutory service-of-process details and the agent's term of appointment. Issue share certificates to the subscriber upon receipt of the subscription consideration, record the issuance in the share register and open the statutory stock ledger.
required_dossiers: Registered agent acknowledgement of appointment
Issued and unissued share certificate forms
Share register and stock ledger
Corporate seal, if the board elected to adopt one
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or the registered office address changes, file a statement of change with the Registrar; a lapsed agency must be replaced immediately to avoid suspension of the corporation's status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Collect Certificate of Incorporation and Deliver the Corporate Compliance Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (issuance) and the licensed registered agent (delivery).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance, verify the certificate of incorporation for accuracy of the corporate name, incorporation date, registered agent and authorised capital. Obtain a certified copy of the endorsed Articles and compile the corporate kit containing the certificate, bylaws, organisational consents, share register and the annual report compliance calendar.
required_dossiers: Original certificate of incorporation
Certified copy of filed Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal and minute book contents
Receipts of government fees and agent fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or Articles contain a scrivener's error, file a certificate of correction with the Registrar for immediate reissuance; any omission in the authorised capital schedule must be cured by a formal amendment of the Articles.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator, Office of the Maritime Administrator, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands; port and lagoon operations are additionally regulated by the Marshall Islands Marine Resources Authority (MIMRA).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Bunkering and Marine Fuel Supplier Permit for the offshore supply of marine gas oil, IFO 380 and lubricants to vessels; issued as a vessel-operations endorsement to the corporation's maritime services licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA), established under the Environmental Protection Act 1984.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) with registration; a full Environmental Impact Assessment is required only for shore-based fuel storage exceeding 500,000 litres, whereas offshore bunker barges are handled by EPA registration accompanied by a spill-contingency plan and the EPA registration certificate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL 73/78 Annex I and Annex V; treated oily-water discharge limited to no more than 10 mg/L oil and grease; no free-fall discharge of fuel or lubricants into lagoon waters; vapour controlled to a maximum of 10% of the lower explosive limit at vent points during transfer; any spill must be reported to the RMI EPA and the Harbormaster within two hours; waste oil may be disposed of only at licensed reception facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Majuro Fire Department covering fixed and portable extinguishing systems and a Class B fire-risk assessment; structural-load inspection and pressure-test certificates for fuel tanks, hoses and transfer arms issued by an RMI-licensed marine surveyor; occupational workplace clearance under RMI health and safety standards requiring crew training, personal flotation devices, documented spill-response drills and a written emergency-response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Revenue and Taxation Division (Majuro); corporate registry function performed by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations (designated registered agent regime). No fully automated national e-filing portal exists; filings are effected through licensed registered agents and the Revenue and Taxation Division.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Foreign principals incorporate a Business Corporation (BC) under the Business Corporations Act (BCA) via a licensed registered agent, obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation whose registration number serves as the de facto corporate identifier. Step 2: File the statutory Non-Resident Domestic Corporation certificate with the Registrar of Corporations, attesting that the BC holds no real property in the Marshall Islands (RMI) and carries on no business within RMI. Step 3: Where a physical TIN is required for banking, customs, or port operations, file TIN application form with the Revenue and Taxation Division; TIN issuance is otherwise administrative and immediate for non-resident BCs. Step 4: Register the foreign beneficial owners and directors in the confidential non-public registry maintained by the registered agent for AML compliance. Step 5: No income tax registration, no VAT registration, and no payroll tax registration are required while the non-resident exemption remains in force.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC). The RMI taxes on a strictly territorial source basis; a BC that validly files the non-resident certificate is wholly exempt from RMI income tax, gross receipts tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, inheritance tax, and stamp duties on offshore transactions. A resident domestic corporation (or foreign corporation) engaged in RMI-source business is instead subject to a gross-receipts tax of 3% (resident domestic) or 4% (foreign corporation), plus applicable municipal business license fees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch or CFC elections exist in RMI tax law. The operative statutory status election is the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation certificate filed under the BCA: the BC must covenant (a) it does not own or lease RMI real property and (b) it does not transact business within RMI. The election remains effective indefinitely while the certificate is on file; engaging in RMI-source activity automatically voids the exemption and exposes the BC to retrospective gross-receipts taxation. There is no separate tax treaty election or entity reclassification mechanism, and the RMI has no double-taxation treaty network.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None - No VAT/GST/Sales-and-Use-Tax regime exists in the Marshall Islands; indirect revenue is collected exclusively through import duties and excises under the Customs Tariff Act. Marine bunkers delivered to vessels in international traffic are treated as ship's stores and are not subject to RMI import duty, provided they do not enter RMI domestic consumption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not Applicable - there is no VAT/GST registration threshold, no sales-and-use-tax registration, and no intrastate turnover threshold. As a reference point for import duty, the Customs Tariff Act applies a 2% standard ad valorem duty on most dutiable imports (higher scheduled rates apply to alcohol, tobacco, petroleum products for domestic use), with no turnover-based de minimis threshold for commercial importers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None - the RMI imposes no electronic invoicing mandate, no real-time fiscal clearance, no SAF-T reporting, no digital stamping, and no fiscal data exchange API for B2B or B2C invoicing. Bunker invoices and delivery receipts are commercial documents governed by contract law and the International Fuel Purchase and Sale Agreement terms; record retention of at least five years applies under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act for AML purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in a strict VAT sense because the RMI imposes no VAT/GST. Equivalent zero-tax treatment for international marine bunkering is achieved through the territorial system: supplies of ISIC 5222 marine fuel and lubricants by a non-resident BC are wholly outside RMI taxing jurisdiction when the sale is negotiated and invoiced offshore, title passes outside RMI customs territory, payment is received into a non-RMI bank account, and the product is delivered as ship's stores to a vessel engaged in international traffic. There is no RMI refund mechanism because there is no input VAT to recover; the effective rate is 0% by statutory exclusion.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bunker Delivery Receipt (BDR) signed by the receiving vessel's chief engineer
Statement of Facts or Delivery Survey Report confirming quantities and vessel identity
Commercial Invoice / Sale and Purchase Note referencing the bunker contract and vessel IMO number
Customs Ship's Stores Permit or Port Clearance (only when delivery occurs within RMI port limits)
Bill of Lading, Mate's Receipt, or Vessel Departure/Arrival Log evidencing international voyage status
Bank MT103 / Swift wire credit confirmation serving as inward remittance evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RMI has no exchange-control regime, so the 180-day target is a documentary integrity benchmark aligned with banking and marine insurance practice rather than a statutory repatriation deadline; funds received offshore need not be repatriated to RMI. Because no VAT exists, there is no export-VAT refund or VAT clawback mechanism. Enforcement exposure concentrates on: (1) Customs fraud - false declarations on ship's stores or dutiable imports trigger forfeiture of goods, monetary penalties up to three times the duty evaded, and imprisonment under the Customs Tariff Act; (2) gross-receipts tax recapture - if an NRDC is found to have derived RMI-source income while the non-resident certificate was on file, the Revenue and Taxation Division may assess 3% (domestic) or 4% (foreign) of gross revenue retrospectively, plus statutory interest and fraud/negligence penalties; (3) regulatory strike-off - the Registrar may revoke the non-resident status certificate or dissolve the BC for misrepresentation, and directors and the registered agent face personal liability for knowingly false filings; and (4)AML penalties - failure to maintain bunkering counterparty due-diligence and transaction records for the statutory retention period attracts fines under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act and can disqualify the BC from RMI ship registration benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) does not operate a domestic central bank. The US dollar is sole legal tender and monetary policy is effectively set by the US Federal Reserve. Banking licensing, AML/CFT supervision, and prudential oversight are administered by the Banking Commissioner within the Ministry of Finance pursuant to the Banking Act 2013 (as amended) and the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2021 (FTRA), which implements the FATF standards.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. The RMI maintains no exchange-control administration, no inward-investment approval, and no profit-remittance permit regime. A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) may freely repatriate dividends, redemption proceeds, loan repayments, and liquidation distributions in USD without tax or exchange levies, provided the underlying transactions are documented and compliant with FTRA record-keeping obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. The RMI imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export or bunkering proceeds. Receipts may be held offshore or in-country at the corporate treasury's discretion; banks will require only standard commercial documentation (commercial invoice, Bunker Delivery Note, and contract) to support each credit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD); Capital Escrow Account available upon regulatory notification
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (USD with US Fedwire and CHIPS clearing access)
Not applicable - statutory development lender; no commercial treasury or cross-border account services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. The RMI has no e-money institution licensing regime and no digital bank has received a license under the Banking Act 2013. Global digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, WorldFirst) generally decline or close accounts for RMI-registered non-resident corporations due to correspondent-bank de-risking, offshore-perception flags, and the high-risk maritime fuel sector. A licensed RMI bank account is therefore a mandatory prerequisite; US-chartered fintech banks may be entertained only if the BC demonstrates a genuine US operating nexus (office, employees, director residency) and a proven compliance track record.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted by Bank of Marshall Islands for non-resident directors and shareholders using an apostilled/notarized corporate packet (Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Registered Agent Certificate, board resolutions, FTRA beneficial-ownership schedule, and passport copies) complemented by live video verification. Bank of Guam, as a US-regulated institution, requires either physical attendance at the Majuro branch or a US-notarized video KYC interview; a physical visit by the ultimate beneficial owner and signatory is strongly recommended and reduces onboarding timeline to 7-10 business days, whereas fully remote processing can extend to 4-6 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Maritime fuel trading flagged as a sanctions/AML high-risk sector under OFAC evasion typologies, including illicit ship-to-ship transfers and bunkering near North Korean or Iranian waters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid bunkering operating license; IMO number and flag-state registration for owned or chartered bunker barges; P&I club certificate; OFAC/SDN screening policy with audit trail; counterparty KYC files and charter parties; ISO 8217 fuel-quality compliance documentation; transaction-flow narrative from purchase order to Bunker Delivery Note; and an intended port list excluding UN-sanctioned zones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, zero-tax offshore entity lacking economic substance (shell-corporation indicator).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-agent Certificate of Good Standing; foreign physical office lease and staff employment contracts; board minutes approving treasury mandate and bank signatories; executed fuel-supply and offtake agreements; prior-year audited financial statements (IFRS or US GAAP) or certified management accounts; and a substance memorandum detailing actual bunker supply operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity or issuance of bearer shares permitted under the RMI Business Corporations Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FTRA-compliant beneficial-ownership schedule identifying all natural-person UBOs; full shareholder register and register of directors; evidence of immobilization of any bearer shares with an RMI-licensed custodian; corporate organizational chart; passport copies, proof of residential address, and professional references for each UBO holding 10% or more.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Uncertain transaction flows and future counterparties located in high-risk or high-tax-haven-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Anticipated-activity questionnaire with 12-month transaction forecast; pre-screened counterparty list (suppliers, brokers, port agents) with sanctions-clearance evidence; sample MT103 remittance narratives using compliant purpose codes; incoterms framework (FOB/CIF); and a written undertaking to provide Bunker Delivery Notes, surveyor reports, and commercial invoices for every drawdown.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: RMI's presence on the EU's Annex II list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions with pending commitments, triggering enhanced adverse-media review and tax-motive presumption.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RMI annual-report filing receipts and Certificate of Good Standing; proof of genuine fuel-supply economic activity differentiating from tax-motive arrangement; CRS/FATCA self-certifications for all UBOs; signed exchange-of-information consent; appointment of an AML compliance officer with training certificates; and a sanctions/ABAC corporate policy manual.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan proceeds must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to the BC's USD account at Bank of Marshall Islands or Bank of Guam. Field 70 remittance information must read 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN' plus the entity reference and, where a Capital Escrow Account is used, the escrow-agreement number. For US-cleared transfers, Fedwire purpose code 'B1' (business) with narrative 'CAP INJ MH_BC' is acceptable. The beneficiary bank must hold on file: board resolution approving the contribution, executed subscription or intercompany loan agreement, UBO source-of-funds declaration with 12-month shareholder bank statements, and an updated share register. No RMI exchange-control or tax approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Open-account bunker purchases are settled by SWIFT MT103 wires with USD cleared via Fedwire or CHIPS for same-day finality; SWIFT MT202 COV is used for correspondent-bank reimbursement. Credit-backed procurement uses usance Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP600, 30-60 days) and Standby Letters of Credit (ISP98/UCP600) issued by Bank of Guam or Bank of Marshall Islands and advised through the supplier's bank (e.g., DBS, Standard Chartered, HSBC) to secure credit lines. Every disbursement must be matched to a Bunker Delivery Note, supplier invoice, and independent survey report; value-date discipline and the relevant USD clearing cut-off (typically 17:00 ET Fedwire / CHIPS cycle) must be observed to avoid failed settlements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, SGD, HKD, and NZD with Bank of Guam or an OECD-licensed international bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW, TWD, INR, PHP, VND, and other restricted Asian currencies to hedge regional bunker procurement, cash-settled in USD
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to convert long-term non-USD supply-purchase or charter-payment obligations into floating or fixed USD
Plain-vanilla FX call and put options for budget protection on AUD, SGD, EUR, and JPY exposures
OTC bunker fuel price swaps and ICE-listed Brent and gasoil futures authorized by board resolution to hedge inventory and procurement price risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Report and Franchise Tax Return (tiered fee by authorized capital)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Maritime and Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 of each calendar year; no grace extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of 10% of the franchise tax if paid after April 30; continued non-payment triggers administrative dissolution and strike-off from the Corporate Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (maintained by the registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the Annual Corporation Report, due April 30 annually; updates required within 30 days of any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for willful non-compliance under the Business Corporations (Amendment) Act 2019; risk of strike-off for persistent failure to confirm UBO details

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Renewal and Registered Office Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent (private contractual filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April 30, aligned with the corporate reporting cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent results in loss of good standing and administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Marine Fuel License / Bunkering Permit Annual Endorsement (if vessel-based supply operations conducted)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of the underlying license issuance; renewal within 90 days prior to expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License suspension, cessation of bunkering operations, and port state control flagging

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a non-resident, privately held Business Corporation; audit mandatory only if shares are publicly listed on a stock exchange or if the Registrar or court requires audited accounts in respect of exempted companies
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory local GAAP; IFRS is the commonly adopted framework when financial statements are voluntarily prepared for lenders, charterers, or tax residency evidence

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Business Corporation must file an annual confirmation statement identifying each beneficial owner, nominee shareholder, and any indirect control chain; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership during the year must be recorded in the internal share register and an updated confirmation must be filed with the registered agent within 30 days
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders incl. transfers and pledge details)
Minute Book of shareholder and board resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per annum standard for non-resident BC
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; if voluntarily prepared for LC-backed shipping finance or charterer counterparties, USD 8,000 - 20,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (non-resident Business Corporation is exempt from Marshall Islands income tax; no corporate profits tax is levied on income derived outside the Republic)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate remains 0% for non-resident BCs. The Marshall Islands does not operate a broad territorial income tax on foreign-source income; qualifying non-resident BCs are outside the income tax base. For vessel operators, MIRA annual tonnage fees and registration costs apply in lieu of corporate income taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No standard CIT return applies to a non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation. Filing obligations are confined to: (1) Annual Report and Franchise Tax filing with the Registrar of Corporations (physical or e-filing through the MARIPO/ online corporate registry); (2) if the entity owns or operates a vessel under the Marshall Islands flag, MIRA vessel registration and annual fee/tonnage reporting; (3) beneficial ownership filing under the Associations and Companies (Amendment) Act 2020.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Report and Franchise Tax payable on or before the anniversary date of incorporation (typically filing deadline is March 31 for calendar-year filers or anniversary date, depending on Registrar practice). Vessel registration renewals are due on MIRA's annual anniversary schedule. Beneficial ownership updates must be filed within 30 days of change.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name, registration number, registered agent name and physical Marshall Islands address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure registered agent availability; if none, the corporation is in default and subject to administrative dissolution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current names, addresses, and shareholdings of each director and shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may be natural or legal persons; bearer shares are not permitted. Details must be current but not publicly-accessible in certain circumstances; however disclosure to the Registrar is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address of principal business office, which may be outside the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a ship fuel supply company, the principal office may be a commercial office in Singapore/Dubai/Monaco; this field should be accurate to align with economic substance expectations and bank AML records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: USD franchise tax schedule based on authorized capital or fixed minimum USD 250 for BCs (exact per Registrar fee schedule).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made from a bank account in the name of the corporation; personal payment may raise AML flags.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Short description of the actual business activity and ISIC code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company must not engage in shipping brokerage or bunker trading activities that require special licensing if such license has not been obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ownership of vessels, bareboat charters, or management agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no vessel is registered under the Marshall Islands flag, state none; if bareboat charter-in is used, disclose MIRA approval for foreign-flag vessels.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that no Marshall Islands source income is derived and that no domestic tax return is filed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain in the corporate records a board resolution and contemporaneous economic substance memo confirming all income is foreign-source; failure to prove this in an audit could lead to deemed income recategorization.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Annual Report and pay franchise tax results in late penalties, interest, automatic administrative dissolution, and reinstatement costs. Failure to update beneficial ownership may lead to criminal penalties under AML legislation. Vessels may be deleted from the Marshall Islands registry for non-payment of MIRA annual fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (no dividend withholding tax is imposed by the Marshall Islands on distributions by a non-resident Business Corporation)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation treaty network. No treaty relief procedure exists for dividends. If a shareholder's home jurisdiction claims a foreign tax credit, the Marshall Islands will provide at most a Certificate of Residency/Tax Residency (issued by the Ministry of Finance / RMI Tax Office) evidencing non-residence; but due to the absence of income tax, no underlying foreign tax credit attaches. Claiming treaty relief based solely on a Marshall Islands entity without substance will be ineffective in a shareholder jurisdiction.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% domestic statutory rate on royalty and interest payments to non-residents; no withholding tax imposed. Because no DTA exists, no treaty-reduced rate is relevant. IP royalties paid to a non-resident BC remain untaxed in the Marshall Islands. However, a foreign payor must apply its domestic source rules.
